subject: Performance SLO / VPC qualification follow-up - ACME
messages:
From: jordan_blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Johnson <claire.johnson@acme.com>, ACME Infra <infra@acme.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: Post-call recap: Performance targets & VPC/network qualification

Thanks again for the call today — great to meet the ACME infra team. Quick recap and next steps so we stay aligned on the performance/SLO and private deployment items we discussed.

Summary of targets (please confirm):
- Latency: 95th percentile P95 <= 120ms for short-chat (<= 64 tokens) when using streaming responses.
- Tail: P99 target <= 300ms across our Dedicated/private footprint.
- Throughput: sustained 400 req/s average during business hours, burst to 800 req/s for short windows.
- Concurrency: expected 150 concurrent sessions (typical chat sessions hold an open streaming connection).
- Streaming: chunked server-sent events, ~50ms chunk cadence preferred for progressive render.

Networking / private deployment notes:
- You mentioned VPC peering & a VPN fallback. We need: IP ranges, preferred peering model (AWS VPC peering vs Transit Gateway), and any egress routing constraints.
- Internal latency budget: please confirm ACME's acceptable network RTT from app servers -> Redwood private endpoint <= 20ms (one-way) to meet the P95 target above.
- MTU, TLS termination, and any proxy/load balancer timeouts that could affect long-lived streaming connections (keepalive recommended >= 120s).

Action items / next steps:
1) ACME infra: share network diagram, egress IP ranges, and a traceroute sample to our test endpoint (we provided a temporary hostname on call).
2) Marcus (tech): will validate streaming configuration and recommend keepalive/timeout settings and a recommended concurrency model.
3) Marissa (sales/solutions): will share a filled SLO matrix and a proposed mutual action plan for the pilot (POC) including test windows.

Attachments: I attached a starter SLO matrix (20270503-acme-slo-matrix.xlsx) with the values we discussed.

If anything above is incorrect or missing, flag it and we'll update. Proposed time for a short network deep-dive: Wed 05/05 10:00 PT.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123
From: Claire Johnson <claire.johnson@acme.com>
To: jordan_blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: ACME Infra <infra@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 04 May 2027 09:04:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Performance targets & VPC/network qualification

Thanks Jordan — this is a great recap. A couple clarifications from our side:
- The 120ms P95 is for application-level latency seen by our frontend. Need to confirm if Redwood's P95 is measured end-to-end or only at the inference service.
- We currently use AWS Transit Gateway for VPC connectivity (not simple peering) and have an egress NAT with static IPs (will share).
- Our internal app tier RTT to the edge LB is typically 8-12ms; to the US-west Redwood region we expect ~18-25ms depending on routing.

I'll loop in infra@acme with the traceroute and config snippets. We can confirm the transit paths before the Wed slot — if not, can we push the network deep-dive to Thu 05/06 09:00 PT?

Claire
Claire Johnson
Head of Platform Engineering, ACME Corp
From: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Johnson <claire.johnson@acme.com>, jordan_blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 05 May 2027 16:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Performance targets & VPC/network qualification

Claire — thanks for the note and context. A few technical clarifications and requests from the infra side: 

1) Measurement point: Redwood's P95/P99 numbers are measured at the inference edge (our private endpoint) including TLS termination and our runtime processing. To map to frontend app-level latency you'll want to add network RTTs and rendering time.

2) Streaming specifics: we use HTTP/1.1 chunked or HTTP/2 server push for streaming. Long-lived connections are kept alive; we recommend keeping LB and proxy idle timeouts >= 120s to avoid premature termination of interactive sessions.

3) Concurrency model: for private deployments we shard sessions across worker pools. Sustained 400 req/s with 150 concurrent streaming sessions is within expected capacity for a single medium cluster, but tail latency depends heavily on network jitter and packet loss.

4) Network asks: please provide:
   - traceroute to redwood-test.us-west.redwood.ai (we got your sample but need a couple across times)
   - NAT egress IPs (for firewall rules)
   - Transit Gateway config (ASN, route tables) or peering preference

5) Quick test we can run (low-touch): run an automated 10-minute streaming load from one of your app nodes to our test endpoint and capture p95/p99 at both client and server side (we'll provide a small harness). This will tell us if the existing routing meets the internal latency budget.

I'll prepare recommended keepalive/timeout settings and a short checklist for the network call.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Systems Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Johnson <claire.johnson@acme.com>, jordan_blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 06 May 2027 13:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Performance targets & VPC/network qualification

Claire — thanks, we're happy to move the deep-dive to Thu 05/06 09:00 PT (confirmed). Attached is an updated SLO matrix with a proposed pilot plan and acceptance criteria. Highlights: 
- Pilot window: 2 weeks of staged load tests with clear escalation points.
- Acceptance: P95 observed at Redwood edge + measured network RTT to be <= 140ms end-to-end for typical short-chat paths.
- Rollout plan: start with a single VPC peering test (if Transit Gateway allows), then expand to full Transit Gateway once traffic steering is validated.

Attachments: 20270503-acme-slo-matrix.xlsx (updated), and I'll post the network deep-dive calendar invite with dial-in.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
From: jordan_blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Johnson <claire.johnson@acme.com>, ACME Infra <infra@acme.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 09 May 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Performance targets & VPC/network qualification

Following up with the artifacts we asked for on the call — thanks for sending the traceroute earlier (attached as 20270505-traceroute-snapshot.txt). Next immediate items for ACME infra:
- Confirm 3 traceroute samples from different AZs (we need variability).
- Provide the Transit Gateway route table snapshot or JSON export.
- Whitelist the 3 egress IPs in the attached SLO matrix for the pilot.

Marcus will send the lightweight test harness and expected client-side metrics so you can run the 10-minute streaming test. Marissa will follow up with the pilot MOP and calendar invite.

If you approve, we'll provision a private test endpoint in the US-West region tomorrow morning and share credentials.

Thanks — Jordan
